answer: Judgment: the >$500m FY26 productivity target is sized as an offset to wage, banker and UNITE pressure, not as a jaws-restorer; the disclosure gives no FY26 revenue guidance, so positive jaws cannot be demonstrated from these documents. The FY25 expense bridge shows FY24 expenses of $10,944m rising to $11,916m: staff +$397m, technology +$146m, volume/other +$199m, investments +$359m and a $273m Fit for Growth restructuring charge, against productivity of -$402m. Expenses rose 9% (6% ex the charge) versus income growth of 3% ($22,464m vs $21,763m) - jaws of roughly -6ppts (-3ppts ex charge, derived); productivity offset only ~37% of the $1,101m gross ex-charge cost growth, and CTI ex Notable Items rose from 50.3% to 53.0%. The investment mix pivoted to UNITE ($147m to $660m) from risk & regulatory ($1,059m to $695m), lifting the expensed share from 56% to 60% of a $1,918m total. For FY26 Westpac flags ~$2bn total investment, UNITE of $850-950m at ~75% expensed, reductions in the other two categories, a moderating (but still positive) amortisation increase, an EBA increase of 3-4% and continued banker investment. UNITE is multi-year: the plan extends into FY29, FY27-FY28 absorb c.40% of c.$2bn p.a. spend, with lower spend only in FY29 and c.75% expensed throughout. Derived from disclosed figures, expensed UNITE rises ~$150-225m in FY26 (74% x $660m = ~$488m to 75% x $850-950m = ~$638-713m); adding wage growth (FY25 staff costs alone rose $397m) the >$500m target - only ~$100m above the $402m delivered in FY25 - roughly matches the identified headwinds. Westpac itself frames closing its CTI gap to peers (3.7ppts above at 1H25) as a Sep-29 outcome via UNITE. Productivity is mainly the funding mechanism that keeps ex-charge expense growth from re-running FY25's 6% while UNITE spend peaks; restoring positive jaws would require income growth above FY25's 3%, on which these documents are silent.

Excluding this charge, operating expenses increased by 6% due to the ramp up in UNITE investment, wage growth and higher software amortisation.

limitations: No FY26 revenue or NIM guidance is disclosed, so FY26 jaws cannot be computed prospectively from these documents.
No aggregate FY26 expense-growth guidance is given; only component flags (EBA 3-4%, UNITE $850-950m, moderating amortisation, lower non-UNITE investment).
The wage (EBA) base within the $6,326m staff expense line is not split out, so the dollar impact of the 3-4% EBA increase cannot be computed.
The documents do not state whether the $273m Fit for Growth restructuring charge recurs in FY26.
The FY25 UNITE expensed share differs between documents (74% in the results announcement vs 76% in the presentation).
The derived $150-225m incremental expensed-UNITE range applies disclosed percentages to disclosed spend; Westpac does not print this figure.
